pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/mcp/src/main.rs:4 lt-mcp is a stateless stdio tool server that forwards calls to the API. It assembles no hook chain, loads no contributed code, holds no agent loop and stores no checkpoints. A case-insensitive search of crates/mcp found no hits for checkpoint, subagent, plugin, middleware or compaction; the only 'hook' hit is 'webhook' in write.rs.

techniques.evidence: crates/mcp/src/main.rs:35 The write gate is an operator/runtime capability, not a client-surface one. stdio runs one session per process. tools/list (tools.rs:26) and tools/call (tools.rs:104) both derive from this one flag plus the contract's mutating bit.

crates/mcp/src/read.rs:90 Exposing job status is the tool server's wire surface. Custody of long-running work belongs to the host agent runtime, which the golden path assigns to this subject, while the server side belongs to mcp-tools.
crates/mcp/src/tools.rs:26 The roster is compiled from a static contract table. No configuration tier can name code to load.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/relay.rs:140 When a device dies mid-run on a relay task (a Claude Code run, possibly edit-mode with an irreversible connector), the task is either leased out again or dead-lettered. The dead-letter status is the same 'dead' a failure-exhausted task gets, distinguished only by the RELAY_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST prefix string in error. The unknown outcome is therefore encoded as a message string inside a failure-class status, and side-effecting work is re-issued.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/relay.rs:140 The device-death outcome has no first-class indeterminate status: the error column carries a marker string (bound at relay.rs:147). The partial conformance is that restarts are counted on their own key (stale_reclaims, relay.rs:173; jobs.rs:77), separate from failures.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path says 'the closed status vocabulary, the lease whose expiry is evidence of a dead executor' belong to job-coordination. But indeterminate-closure-on-interruption's own decision rules govern exactly that store-level reclaim: 'count restarts on a key of their own', 'classify against the liveness threshold', and 'what status a killed run is given'. The seam between the two subjects needs stating, so that storage contexts reclaiming agent runs know which standard binds.

pairs.subject: agent-runtime-assembly
pairs.evidence: clients/python/lighttrack/instrument.py:236 The auto-instrument wrapper runs the refusing admission gate before the journal breadcrumb (line 238) and the span recorder. With enforce='block' and the default record_blocked=False, every refused call raises with no event recorded, so the ledger is blind on exactly the refused calls.

techniques.evidence: clients/python/lighttrack/instrument.py:236 The receipt stamper sits inside the gate. Recording blocked calls is opt-in (client.py:246, record_blocked: bool = False), which is the gapped-ledger failure mode.

clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:442 Calls recovered after a crash are closed with the failure status. Unknown is carried only by an error string and the RECOVERED_TAG tag, not by a first-class indeterminate status.

clients/python/lighttrack/client.py:505 There is no contributed-extension registration surface. The refusal is a typed exception surfaced to the host app, a deliberate choice documented at instrument.py:232-235.
